title: Who says it? and longer texts

blurb.en: Match ideas to the right child, then read longer magazine texts for feelings and plans.
blurb.vi: Tìm đúng bạn nhỏ cho mỗi ý, rồi đọc bài tạp chí dài hơn để tìm cảm xúc và kế hoạch.

paraphrase.vi: diễn đạt lại bằng từ khác
paraphrase.def: Saying the same idea again with different words.
paraphrase.ex: 'I had a high fever' is a *paraphrase* of 'I was ill'.

key idea.def: The most important part of a question, the thing you must look for.
key idea.ex: In 'Which person missed a show?', the *key idea* is 'missed'.

similar.def: Almost the same, but not exactly the same.
similar.ex: All three texts are *similar*: each child talks about being ill.

compare.def: To look at two or more things to see how they are the same or different.
compare.ex: *Compare* the three texts before you choose a name.

nervous.def: A little worried or afraid before something happens.
nervous.ex: I was *nervous* before I sang in front of the class.

disappointed.def: Sad because something did not happen the way you hoped.
disappointed.ex: She was *disappointed* when the trip was cancelled.

proud.def: Pleased about something good that you or someone close to you did.
proud.ex: He is *proud* of the cake he baked.

relieved.def: Happy because a worry or a problem has ended.
relieved.ex: I was *relieved* when my lost cat came home.

confident.def: Sure that you can do something well.
confident.ex: After lots of practice, she felt *confident* on stage.

magazine.def: A thin book with articles and pictures that comes out every week or month.
magazine.ex: Our school *magazine* has a page about children's hobbies.

paragraph.def: A short group of sentences about one idea. A new one starts on a new line.
paragraph.ex: The answer to question 2 is in the second *paragraph*.

introduction.vi: lời giới thiệu, phần mở đầu
introduction.def: The first line or part of a text that tells you what it is about.
introduction.ex: Read the *introduction* under the title first.

opinion.def: What a person thinks or believes about something.
opinion.ex: In my *opinion*, the second story was better.

plan.def: Something you have decided to do in the future.
plan.ex: Her *plan* is to write a second book next year.

scenes.head: Part 5: three children write about animals
scenes.html:
Ollie: My cat sleeps all day. I'd love a dog too, but our flat is too small.

Tia: I've got two rabbits. I feed them every morning before school.

Son: I haven't got a pet, but I *walk my neighbour's dog* every Sunday.

Question: Which person *looks after an animal that isn't theirs*?

steps.en: Read the *question* first. The key idea is 'an animal that isn't theirs'.
steps.vi: Đọc *câu hỏi* trước. Ý chính là 'một con vật không phải của bạn ấy'.

steps.en: All three children talk about animals. That is normal in Part 5: the texts are *similar*.
steps.vi: Cả ba bạn đều nói về động vật. Ở Phần 5 điều này rất bình thường: các đoạn văn *giống nhau*.

steps.en: Ollie and Tia look after their *own* pets. Son walks his *neighbour's* dog.
steps.vi: Ollie và Tia chăm sóc thú cưng *của mình*. Son dắt chó *của hàng xóm* đi dạo.

steps.en: So the answer is Son. Always check *all three* texts before you choose.
steps.vi: Vậy đáp án là Son. Luôn kiểm tra *cả ba* đoạn văn trước khi chọn.

scenes.head: A Part 5 question and one text
scenes.html:
Question: Which person has *changed their mind* about a food?

Daisy: I *used to hate* mushrooms. My dad cooked them in a soup last winter, and *now I ask for them* every time we eat out.

steps.en: The question says 'changed their mind'. Daisy never uses those words.
steps.vi: Câu hỏi nói 'changed their mind' (đổi ý). Daisy không hề dùng những từ đó.

steps.en: But 'I *used to hate*' and '*now I ask for them*' show the same idea. This is a *paraphrase*.
steps.vi: Nhưng 'I *used to hate*' (trước đây ghét) và '*now I ask for them*' (bây giờ lại xin ăn) cùng ý. Đây là *diễn đạt lại*.

steps.en: Look for the *meaning*, not the same words.
steps.vi: Hãy tìm *ý nghĩa*, không tìm những từ giống hệt.

scenes.head: Part 6: from a magazine article
scenes.html: *Tia's friends thought* the school play would be boring, but Tia didn't agree. *At first*, she was nervous about her lines. *In the end*, she loved being on stage. *Her drama teacher said* her voice was clear and strong. Next year, Tia *hopes to* write her own play.

steps.en: 'Tia's friends thought' is the *friends'* opinion, not Tia's. Wrong options often use other people's ideas.
steps.vi: 'Tia's friends thought' là ý kiến của *các bạn*, không phải của Tia. Đáp án sai thường dùng ý của người khác.

steps.en: *At first* and *in the end* show a feeling that *changed*: nervous, then happy.
steps.vi: *At first* (lúc đầu) và *in the end* (cuối cùng) cho thấy cảm xúc *đã thay đổi*: lo lắng, rồi vui.

steps.en: 'Her drama teacher said' gives an *adult's* opinion. 'Hopes to' shows a *plan*.
steps.vi: 'Her drama teacher said' cho biết ý kiến của *người lớn*. 'Hopes to' cho biết một *kế hoạch*.

end.en: Brilliant! You can find the key idea, compare texts and spot whose idea it is.
end.vi: Tuyệt vời! Bạn biết tìm ý chính, so sánh các đoạn văn và nhận ra đó là ý của ai.

challenge.result: You spotted paraphrases, feelings and other people's ideas.

v.q: 'When I saw the price, I couldn't believe my eyes!' How did the writer feel?
opts: very surprised
a little bit worried
a bit bored
whys: Nothing in the sentence shows that the writer was worried.
'Couldn't believe my eyes' shows a strong feeling, not boredom.
v.hint: Think about when people say 'I can't believe it'.
v.worked: 'I *couldn't believe my eyes*' means the writer was very surprised.

v.q: 'When we won the match, I was over the moon!' How did the writer feel?
opts: extremely happy
a little scared
quite sleepy
whys: Winning a match doesn't usually make people scared.
'Over the moon' is a strong feeling, not a sleepy one.
v.hint: Think about how you feel when your team wins.
v.worked: 'I was *over the moon*' means the writer was extremely happy.

v.q: 'Lan's friends thought the film was too long, but Lan loved every minute.' What did Lan think?
opts: She enjoyed all of the film.
She thought it was too long.
She left before the end.
whys: 'Too long' is what Lan's FRIENDS thought.
Lan 'loved every minute', so she watched it all.
v.hint: Find Lan's name. Is the opinion hers or her friends'?
v.worked: 'Lan *loved every minute*' means she enjoyed all of it.

v.q: 'Jamal's dad says the new pool is too cold. Jamal thinks it's the best pool in town.' What is Jamal's opinion?
opts: The pool is great.
The pool is too cold.
The pool is too new.
whys: 'Too cold' is his DAD's opinion.
Nobody says the pool is too new.
v.hint: Two people give an opinion. Which one is Jamal's?
v.worked: 'Jamal thinks it's *the best pool in town*.'

v.q: Ollie: 'I'd love to try surfing one day.' Daisy: 'I went surfing last summer.' Who has already been surfing?
opts: Daisy
Ollie
both of them
whys: Ollie would like to try it 'one day', so he hasn't done it yet.
Only one of them has done it already.
v.hint: Look at the verb forms: 'I'd love to' or 'I went'?
v.worked: Daisy says 'I *went surfing* last summer'. Ollie only wants to try it.

v.q: Son: 'I've never been on a plane.' Tia: 'I fly to see my aunt every year.' Who travels by plane?
opts: Tia
Son
both of them
whys: Son says he has NEVER been on a plane.
Only one of them flies.
v.hint: Look for 'never' and 'every year'.
v.worked: Tia says 'I *fly* to see my aunt *every year*'.

v.q: Which sentence tells you about a plan?
opts: Next summer, I hope to learn to dive.
Last summer, I learned to dive.
I'm good at diving now.
whys: 'Last summer' and 'learned' are about the past.
'Now' tells you about the present, not a plan.
v.hint: Plans are about the future. Look for words like 'next' and 'hope to'.
v.worked: '*Next summer*, I *hope to* learn to dive' is a plan.

v.q: Which sentence tells you that a feeling changed?
opts: At first I was scared, but now I love it.
I have always loved riding horses.
I was scared, and I still am.
whys: 'Always' means the feeling never changed.
'I still am' means the feeling is the same.
v.hint: Look for 'at first' and 'now' in the same sentence.
v.worked: '*At first* I was scared, but *now* I love it': the feeling changed.

blurb.en: Spot paraphrases, compare three short texts and read for feelings and plans.
blurb.vi: Nhận ra cách diễn đạt lại, so sánh ba đoạn ngắn và đọc để tìm cảm xúc, kế hoạch.

v.q: Ollie: 'I couldn't wait for the school trip to start.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Ollie was excited about the trip.
Ollie was worried about the trip.
Ollie didn't want to wait for the bus.
whys: 'Couldn't wait' is a happy feeling, not a worried one.
Nothing is said about a bus: 'couldn't wait' is about a feeling.
v.hint: 'I couldn't wait' is a fixed phrase. How do you feel before something you want?
v.worked: 'I *couldn't wait*' means Ollie was very excited.

v.q: Tia: 'I didn't expect to enjoy the cooking class, but it was great fun.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: The class was better than Tia thought it would be.
Tia knew the class would be fun.
Tia didn't enjoy the cooking class.
whys: 'I didn't expect to enjoy it' means she didn't know it would be fun.
She says it was 'great fun', so she did enjoy it.
v.hint: Find what Tia expected, then what really happened.
v.worked: 'I *didn't expect* to enjoy it, but it was *great fun*': it was better than she thought.

v.q: Son: 'My bike had a flat tyre, so I walked to the park.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Son couldn't ride, so he went on foot.
Son rode his bike to the park.
Son's bike broke in the park.
whys: The tyre was flat, so he walked.
The tyre was flat BEFORE he went, not in the park.
v.hint: Find the word 'so'. What happened because of the flat tyre?
v.worked: 'My bike had a flat tyre, *so I walked*': he went on foot.

v.q: Daisy: 'I stayed at home because I had a sore throat.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Daisy was ill, so she didn't go out.
Daisy went out with a sore throat.
Daisy's throat hurt after she went out.
whys: She 'stayed at home', so she didn't go out.
Her throat hurt first; she didn't go out at all.
v.hint: Find 'because'. It tells you the reason.
v.worked: 'I *stayed at home because* I had a sore throat': she was ill and stayed in.

v.q: Lan: 'Hardly anyone came to the first meeting.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: Very few people came.
Nobody came at all.
Lots and lots of people came.
whys: 'Hardly anyone' means a few people, not zero.
'Hardly anyone' means the opposite of lots.
v.hint: 'Hardly anyone' is not the same as 'nobody'. Think carefully.
v.worked: '*Hardly anyone*' means very few people.

v.q: Adam: 'None of my friends had tried it before.' Which sentence means the same?
opts: It was new for all of his friends.
Some of his friends had tried it already.
All of his friends had tried it.
whys: 'None' means not one friend, so not 'some'.
'None' is the opposite of 'all of them had tried it'.
v.hint: What does 'none' mean: zero, a few or all?
v.worked: '*None* of my friends had tried it': it was new for every friend.

title.vi: Bạn nào? So sánh ba đoạn văn

v.q: Which person couldn't do what they wanted?
opts: Ollie
Daisy
Son
whys: Daisy swam in her aunt's pool all afternoon, so she did what she wanted.
Son played football and swam in the river.
v.hint: All three talk about swimming. Who wanted to swim but couldn't?
v.worked: Ollie: 'I *wanted to swim*, but the sea was *too rough*.'

stim.head: Three children write about their Saturday
stim.html:
Ollie: On Saturday I went to the beach with my parents. I wanted to swim, but the sea was too rough.

Daisy: On Saturday I visited my aunt. We swam in her pool all afternoon.

Son: On Saturday I played football with my friends. Afterwards, we swam in the river.

v.q: Which person has changed their opinion of a food?
opts: Lan
Tia
Kira
whys: Tia has always loved pho: it's her favourite food.
Kira loves pho; she only eats it in a different place.
v.hint: Look for words that show then and now.
v.worked: Lan: 'I *didn't like* pho when I was little, but *now* I eat it every week.'

stim.head: Three children write about pho
stim.html:
Tia: My favourite food is pho. My dad makes it every Sunday.

Kira: I love pho, but I only eat it in restaurants.

Lan: I didn't like pho when I was little, but now I eat it every week.

v.q: Which person joined a club to change something about themselves?
opts: Poppy
Adam
Jamal
whys: Adam joined because of his best friend, not to change himself.
Jamal couldn't join because of his swimming lesson.
v.hint: Find each child's reason. Look after 'because'.
v.worked: Poppy: 'I joined the drama club because I want to be *less shy*.'

stim.head: Three children write about the drama club
stim.html:
Adam: I joined the drama club because my best friend is in it.

Poppy: I joined the drama club because I want to be less shy.

Jamal: I wanted to join the drama club, but it's on Tuesdays and I have swimming then.

v.q: Which person missed school because they were ill?
opts: Son
Quan
Daisy
whys: Quan had a cold, but he still went to school.
Daisy's sister was ill, not Daisy.
v.hint: Two children talk about being ill. Who stayed away from school?
v.worked: Son: 'I had a fever, so I *stayed in bed* for three days.'

stim.head: Three children write about being ill
stim.html:
Quan: I had a cold last week, but I still went to school.

Son: I had a fever, so I stayed in bed for three days. I missed a science test!

Daisy: My sister had a bad cough, so we didn't go to the zoo.

v.q: Which person describes how their street has changed?
opts: Kira
Ollie
Tia
whys: Ollie describes his street now; he doesn't say it was different before.
Tia talks about the noise and lights now, not before.
v.hint: Look for 'used to' or 'there was'. They talk about the past.
v.worked: Kira: 'There *used to be* a toy shop in my street, but *now* it's a bank.'

stim.head: Three children write about their street
stim.html:
Kira: There used to be a toy shop in my street, but now it's a bank.

Ollie: My street is quiet. There's a small park where I play after school.

Tia: My street is very busy, but I like the noise and the lights.

v.q: Which person didn't enjoy one part of their celebration?
opts: Lan
Jamal
Adam
whys: Jamal says nothing bad about his picnic.
Adam had no party, but he doesn't say he was unhappy.
v.hint: Look for a word that shows a problem or a bad feeling.
v.worked: Lan: 'It was *too noisy*!'

stim.head: Three children write about their birthday
stim.html:
Jamal: For my birthday, we had a picnic by the river.

Lan: For my birthday, I invited my whole class to a party. It was too noisy!

Adam: I didn't have a party this year. I went to the cinema with Dad instead.

title.en: Longer texts: feelings, reasons and plans
title.vi: Bài dài hơn: cảm xúc, lý do và kế hoạch

v.q: How did Kira's feelings change?
opts: She expected to be bored, but she loved it.
She was excited, but then she got bored.
She was bored, so she stopped asking questions.
whys: It was the other way round: bored first, then happy.
She asked 'so many questions' that the guide laughed.
v.hint: Find what Kira thought BEFORE the trip, then how she felt at the end.
v.worked: 'She *thought it would be boring*... she told everyone it was *the best trip of the year*.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: When Kira's class went to the science museum, she thought it would be boring. But the guide let her hold a real dinosaur bone, and she asked so many questions that the guide laughed. On the bus home, she told everyone it was the best trip of the year.

v.q: How did Adam feel at the end of the week?
opts: He loved the camp and wanted to stay.
He was still scared of the frogs.
He was excited to go home to his family.
whys: He was only scared on the first night, before he knew about the frogs.
He 'didn't want to go home'.
v.hint: Read the last sentence. It tells you about the end of the week.
v.worked: 'By the end of the week, Adam *didn't want to go home*.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: Adam was excited about his first night at summer camp. But when the lights went out, he heard strange noises and felt scared. His tent partner told him the noises were only frogs. By the end of the week, Adam didn't want to go home.

v.q: Why didn't Quan play in the match?
opts: His ankle needed time to get better.
The coach wanted him to count goals.
He didn't want to play on a Saturday.
whys: Counting goals is what he did INSTEAD; it isn't the reason.
Nothing in the text says he didn't want to play.
v.hint: Find 'the doctor told him'. The reason is near it.
v.worked: 'He had *hurt his ankle*... and the doctor told him to *rest* it.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: Quan's football team had a match on Saturday, but he didn't play. He had hurt his ankle the week before, and the doctor told him to rest it. So he sat with the coach and helped to count the goals.

v.q: Why did Poppy make a card?
opts: She couldn't pay for a big bunch of flowers.
Her mum asked her for a poem.
The flower shop was closed.
whys: Mum didn't ask for anything; the poem was Poppy's idea.
The shop was open: Poppy bought one flower there.
v.hint: Find 'So'. What happened just before it?
v.worked: 'She *didn't have enough money*. So she bought one flower and made a card.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: Poppy wanted to buy her mum a big bunch of flowers for her birthday. When she got to the shop, she didn't have enough money. So she bought one flower and made a card with a poem inside. Mum said it was the best present she had ever had.

v.q: What did the teacher think of the model?
opts: She liked the small details most.
She thought the model was too small.
She wanted it to have moving water.
whys: 'Too small' is what Jamal's FRIENDS thought.
Moving water is Jamal's plan for his next model.
v.hint: Three people have ideas in this text. Find the teacher's words.
v.worked: 'Their teacher said *the tiny details were the best thing* about it.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: Jamal and his friends made a model of a lost city for the school science fair. His friends thought it was too small, but their teacher said the tiny details were the best thing about it. Jamal now wants to make a bigger model with moving water.

v.q: What does Lan want to do with her book?
opts: Give a copy to each person in her family.
Sell it at the school fair.
Write a second recipe book.
whys: Selling it is her FRIENDS' idea. Lan isn't sure about it.
The text doesn't talk about a second book.
v.hint: Lan's friends have one idea. What would LAN rather do?
v.worked: 'She would rather *make one copy for each person in her family*, as a present.'

stim.head: From a magazine article
stim.html: Lan has written a recipe book of her family's favourite dishes. Her friends say she should sell it at the school fair. Lan isn't sure. She would rather make one copy for each person in her family, as a present for the New Year.

blurb.en: Answer 'Which person?' questions, then read longer magazine articles.
blurb.vi: Trả lời câu hỏi 'Bạn nào?', rồi đọc các bài tạp chí dài hơn.

v.q: Which person couldn't go somewhere because someone in the family was ill?
opts: Poppy
Quan
Adam
whys: Quan's cousin had a cold, but Quan still went to the party and sang.
Nobody is ill in Adam's text: his problem was the missing sugar.
v.hint: Find an illness in each text. Then check WHO could not go somewhere.
v.worked: Poppy: 'my baby brother had *a high fever* the day before, so *we couldn't go*.'

stim.head: Part 5: a magazine page
stim.html:
A celebration that didn't go to plan

Adam
Last month it was my dad's birthday, and I wanted to make him a chocolate cake on my own. I followed a recipe from Grandma's old cookbook, but I was in a hurry and I forgot to add the sugar! The cake looked perfect, but it tasted terrible. I was really upset. Dad just laughed and ate two big pieces anyway. He said it was the thought that counted. After that day, I asked Mum if I could join a baking class. Now I go every Saturday, and I always read the recipe twice.

Poppy
Every year, my family goes to the city centre on New Year's Eve to watch the fireworks. This year, my baby brother had a high fever the day before, so we couldn't go. At first, I was so disappointed that I didn't want to talk to anyone. Then Dad had an idea. We made hot chocolate, wrapped ourselves in blankets and watched the fireworks from the balcony of our flat. They were small and far away, but we were all together. To be honest, it was the cosiest New Year ever.

Quan
At the end of term, our class had a party, and I agreed to sing a song. My cousin was going to play the guitar for me, but he had a bad cold, so I had to sing alone. When I stood up, I forgot the words of the second verse! My face went red and I wanted to run away. Then my best friend started singing with me, and soon the whole class joined in. Afterwards, my teacher said that everybody gets nervous, even famous singers. Next term, I'm going to try again.

v.q: Which person missed an event they had prepared for?
opts: Lan
Jamal
Kira
whys: Jamal went to the party; he was ill AFTER it, not before.
Kira went on the camping trip; the bites came during it.
v.hint: Which child was ill BEFORE something they had practised for?
v.worked: Lan: 'It was the week of our *school dance show*... I *had practised so hard*.'

stim.head: Part 5: a magazine page
stim.html:
The week I was ill

Lan
In March, I had a terrible cough and a fever. It was the week of our school dance show, and I was in the front row. The doctor said I needed to stay in bed for five days. I cried, because I had practised so hard. My friend recorded the whole show on her mum's phone, and we watched it together when I felt better. I learned that my body needs rest when it is tired. Now I go to bed at nine o'clock, even at the weekend.

Kira
Last summer, my family went camping by a lake. I didn't want to use the insect repellent, because I hate the smell. That was a big mistake! The next morning, I had twenty mosquito bites on my arms and legs. They were so itchy that I couldn't sleep. Mum took me to a doctor, who gave me some cream. Now I always use repellent, even though it smells bad. I also made a poster for my class about how to stop mosquito bites.

Jamal
At my cousin's birthday party, I ate far too many sweets and three pieces of cake. That night I had a terrible stomach ache, and I felt dizzy when I stood up. The next day, Grandpa made me a bowl of rice soup with a pinch of ginger. It was simple, but it made me feel much better. Grandpa told me that our bodies need fruit, vegetables and protein, not just sugar. Now I eat an apple or a banana after school instead of sweets.

v.q: Which person started to learn a new skill after the day?
opts: Adam
Quan
Poppy
whys: Quan wants to try singing again, but singing isn't new for him.
Poppy's dad had a new idea, but Poppy didn't start learning anything.
v.hint: Look at the END of each text. What does each child do after the day?
v.worked: Adam: 'I asked Mum if I could *join a baking class*. Now I go every Saturday.'

Lan
Jamal

Ten-year-old Son found a clever way to share Tet with his cousins in London.

Son's aunt and uncle live in London with his two cousins. Last December, his older cousin sent him a message: 'I've never seen a real Tet celebration.' That gave Son an idea. He would show them Tet on a video call.

First, Son wanted to call at midnight, so his cousins could watch the fireworks. Then he checked the time difference. London is seven hours behind Vietnam, so midnight in Hanoi is five o'clock in the afternoon there. His cousins would still be at their swimming lesson!

At first, the time differences confused Son, but soon he found the maths fun. In the end, he chose six o'clock in the evening, during the family feast. In London, it was eleven in the morning, and his cousins were free.

On the call, Son showed his cousins the peach blossom and the decorations. Grandma explained that the sticky rice cakes are boiled for ten hours. Afterwards, Son's mum said his plan was so well organised that she didn't need to help at all.

Now Son's cousins want to come to Vietnam for the next Tet. Son is already making a list of places to show them. He also hopes they will teach him about British celebrations.

During the summer holidays, Tia created a magical place and filled a book with it.

Last summer, Tia stayed with her grandparents in a small village in the mountains. There was no internet there. Then it rained for three days, so Tia found some paper and coloured pencils and started to draw a map of an island that didn't exist.

She called it Moon Island. It had a purple forest, a mysterious cave and an enormous waterfall that flowed up into the sky. At first, Tia thought her ideas were silly. But her little brother loved them and asked for a new Moon Island story every night.

By the end of the holiday, Tia had ten stories. Her school was having a writing competition, but at first she didn't want to enter, because she thought her handwriting was too messy. Her grandfather helped her to write more slowly, and she copied out her best story neatly.

Her teacher said the descriptions in the story were incredible. 'I could almost see the purple trees,' she said. Tia didn't win the competition, but her story is now in the school library.

Now Tia is writing a second book, about a lost city under the sea near Moon Island. This time, she wants to draw all the pictures herself.
